Subject: Mamenchisaurus
Brief: A long, largely horizontal sauropod mount. Two separated support islands leave a 7 m cross-passage through the reserved bay. Keep the passage clear above 2.8 m; validate the final neck, tail and supports before installation.

Subject: Tarbosaurus
Brief: A tall theropod mount, read from the connecting walk and the north overlook. Orient the long axis along Z. Reserve the full tail sweep inside the envelope.

Subject: Armoured dinosaur
Brief: Armour, tail mechanics and defensive body plans. No moving parts are supplied; use a separate animation clip later.

Subject: Protoceratops
Brief: A family-scale mount with a lower reading rail. Its envelope intentionally leaves the dinosaur entrance unobstructed.

Subject: Trackway casting
Brief: A shallow, accessible examination surface for a trackway cast. The display table is already built; add only the geological exhibit.

Subject: Comparative teeth
Brief: A side-facing cabinet above the ramp. Compare feeding adaptations using original tooth models. Keep all geometry inside the shallow case.

Subject: Australian megafauna
Brief: Reserve for a Diprotodon or another Australian megafaunal subject. Label its different time period explicitly; do not call every prehistoric animal a dinosaur.

Subject: Pterosaur
Brief: Suspended pterosaur allowance. It is not a dinosaur. Model rigging separately, check supports against roof ribs, and keep the entire envelope above visitor head height.

Subject: Fossil comparison
Brief: An overlook-level comparison table. The shell includes the table and guardrails; add fossil specimens only.

Subject: Butterfly diversity
Brief: Pinned-specimen composition in a shallow wall cabinet. Use separate small models, or an original baked specimen atlas for distant views. No specimen artwork is supplied.

Subject: Beetle diversity
Brief: A second framed collection wall with warm conservation-style presentation. Design allowances are not real conservation specifications.

Subject: Insect Hall of Fame theme
Brief: An island vitrine for insect superlatives. Confirm any eventual largest/heaviest/longest claim with a species-specific source before adding final labels.

Subject: Insect classification
Brief: Low comparison table for body plan models. Deliberately separate insect classification from the eight-legged gallery next door.

Subject: Green tree ant colony
Brief: Empty habitat enclosure. You will supply nest, branches, substrate, ant meshes and animation. This is not a live-animal husbandry design.

Subject: Mantid habitat
Brief: Wall-side enclosure reserved for mantid, branches and foliage. No placeholder insects or greenery are included.

Subject: Aquatic invertebrates
Brief: An aquarium-format shell with a dry, empty interior. Add water and invertebrates later; avoid nested transmissive surfaces in the final GLB.

Subject: Decomposer habitat
Brief: An empty ecological exhibit for leaf litter and decomposer invertebrates. Habitat dressing remains part of your Blender stage.

Subject: Insect body systems
Brief: A deliberately enlarged anatomical model. Display its scale multiplier on the future label so visitors do not confuse model size with animal size.

Subject: Insect mouthparts
Brief: Enlarged comparative mouthparts inside an island vitrine. Include chewing, piercing or other forms only after choosing referenced species.

Subject: Life cycles
Brief: A chronological specimen sequence. The cabinet and typography frame are present; model the lifecycle stages in Blender.

Subject: Pollination
Brief: A teaching-table allowance for insect–flower relationships. Flowers and insects are both intentionally omitted.

Subject: Arachnid comparison
Brief: A comparison vitrine introducing arachnids. Use accurate leg counts and label specimens independently from insects.

Subject: Tarantula enclosure
Brief: An empty quarantine-themed enclosure. No fictional biosecurity system is presented as a working or legally compliant facility.

Subject: Local spider enclosure
Brief: An enclosure for a chosen locally occurring spider. Final species, location and safety interpretation must be researched before publication.

Subject: Web structures
Brief: A backlit web-study cabinet. Supply the silk geometry or baked transparent texture; keep the future exhibit readable without bloom.

Subject: Triceratops
Brief: The feature-gallery mount with a full walk-around route. Inspired by the idea of Melbourne’s Triceratops gallery; this is not a model or reproduction of Horridus.

Subject: Fossil preparation
Brief: A wall-case allowance for preparation tools, rock matrix and fossil evidence. All these assets are left for Blender.

Subject: Handling collection
Brief: A school-group table for tactile or digital models. The runtime interaction is a readable design card, not a finished scientific activity.

Subject: Microscope station
Brief: Reserve for microscope and specimen-tray assets. Do not export room furniture with the specimen GLB.

Subject: Botanical installation
Brief: An empty central planting bed. Trees, ferns, ground cover and fauna are excluded from this delivery. This is a quiet light-court interpretation, not the real Forest Gallery.
